title: NAT and PAT: how the internal network reaches the internet

videos.script: Every machine in the office has a private address, like 10.20.10.21. Nobody on the internet can send a packet to that address. It is not routed out there. {{private}} And yet the office browses the web all day. The trick is in the router. {{router}} When a packet leaves, the router rewrites its source. The private address comes out, and the office's one public address goes in. When the answer comes back, the router puts the private address back. That is NAT. {{rewrite}} In this lesson you watch a ping cross the router and see the address change on the way. {{capture}} Then three PCs connect at once through that one address. You read the router's table and see how it keeps them apart, by port. That is PAT. {{table}} Then you open a door the other way: a port on the public address that leads to a server inside. {{forward}} And you see what NAT costs. It breaks the idea that any machine can reach any other, and there is one thing it cannot do even inside the office. {{costs}}
